description: the OpenAI-shaped HTTP surface the rust harness serves under --serve, and that common/serving.py calls

paths.GET /v1/health: 200 with a JSON body. Every caller checks the status code and nothing else, so the body is informational.
paths.POST /v1/chat/completions: one completion, whole; see request and response below

notes.model_is_ignored: The served checkpoint is a command-line argument, so there is nothing in the request to select. common/serving.py sends the literal "default" and interp/steering/scorecard.py omits the field entirely; both must work, which is why it is optional rather than merely unused.
notes.no_streaming: stream: true is refused with 400 rather than answered with a whole body. No interp client streams, and silently returning a non-streamed response would misreport what happened. If a streaming client ever appears, harness/src/stream.rs already carries a chunk streamer whose drop-the-receiver cancellation is an HTTP client disconnect.
notes.status_codes: post_chat maps 4xx to ServingError (terminal) and 5xx to ServingTransientError (retryable), so the split decides whether a caller retries. Anything the client must fix -- bad JSON, an unknown role, an out-of-range sampling value, a stream request -- is 400. A generation failure is 500.
notes.per_request_seed: seed selects the sampler's stream for that request alone. Two requests carrying the same seed sample alike however many requests ran between them, which a server holding one long-lived sampler could not promise. Absent, it falls back to the --seed the process was started with.
notes.usage_is_real: prompt_tokens counts the encoded prompt and completion_tokens the tokens returned, which excludes the EOS that ended the turn. Callers record these into eval and scorecard artifacts, so zeros would be a silent falsehood rather than a missing field.
notes.concurrency: One generation at a time: runtime Model is Send but not Sync and every generation path takes &mut self. Chat requests serialize behind a mutex the health handler never takes, so a health probe answers during a reply that may run for minutes. The registry entry records concurrency=1.
notes.not_a_compose_service: Unlike the llama.cpp and vLLM entries, this one is a binary the human starts. swap_model refuses it by name (common/serving.py NON_COMPOSE_SERVICES) rather than running docker compose against a service that does not exist.
notes.http_subset: HTTP/1.1 with a Content-Length body only. No keep-alive -- every response closes the connection -- and a chunked request body is refused rather than mis-parsed. urllib, which is what every caller uses, sends neither.
